## 1️⃣ **Jira vs Trello** (most common mistake)

### Overlap
Both can:
- Track tasks
- Show boards (Kanban-style)
- Assign owners & due dates

### ❌ Do NOT buy both when:
- Team is small
- Work is informal
- No audits / workflows / SLAs needed

| Choose | When |
|---|---|

**Rule of thumb:**  
> If you feel Jira is “heavy”, Trello is enough.  
> If Trello feels “too loose”, move to Jira — not both.

---

## 2️⃣ **Jira vs Jira Service Management (JSM)**

### Overlap
Both can:
- Track tickets
- Assign owners
- Show workflows

### ❌ Do NOT buy both when:
- You only track internal work
- No external customers or IT requests

| Choose | When |
|---|---|
| **Jira** | Internal delivery, projects, ops |
| **entity["company","Jira Service Management","it service platform"]** | IT support, incidents, change mgmt |

**Key distinction:**  
> Jira = *delivery*  
> JSM = *support & service*

---

### Overlap (perceived, not real)
- Both allow comments
- Both attach files
- Both show context

### ❌ Do NOT replace Confluence with Jira when:
- Knowledge must live long-term
- Decisions need explanation
- Onboarding matters

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **entity["company","Jira","issue tracking software"]** | Track execution |

> **They do NOT substitute each other.**

| Choose | When |
|---|---|

| GitHub | Open source / community focus |

Both extend Jira / Confluence.

|---|---|

| Choose | When |
|---|---|

| Choose | When |

- ❌ You do **not** need an external web app for UI

- Jira admin pages
- Confluence macros
- Modal dialogs

- Background enrichment only
- No human interaction needed

**Can developers build using Forge GUI like Salesforce? — precise answer**

image_group{"query":["Forge Custom UI React Jira","Forge UI Kit components","Salesforce Lightning App Builder","Salesforce Developer Console Apex"]}

### Short answer
**❌ No — Forge does NOT provide a browser-based “click-to-build” GUI like Salesforce Lightning App Builder.**  
**✅ Yes — developers absolutely use Forge to build GUIs**, but **they do it as code**, not drag-and-drop.

This is a **deliberate design choice** by Atlassian.

---

## 1️⃣ How Salesforce works (baseline comparison)

In **entity["software_platform","Salesforce","crm platform"]** you get:
- **Lightning App Builder** (drag & drop UI)
- **Developer Console** (Apex, SOQL)
- Metadata-driven UI composition
- Heavy browser-based tooling

👉 Salesforce optimizes for **low-code + admin-led development**.

---

## 2️⃣ How Forge works (important difference)

In **entity["software_platform","Forge","atlassian app platform"]**:

### ❌ What Forge does NOT have
- No drag-and-drop UI builder
- No in-browser visual designer
- No admin-style page composer

### ✅ What Forge DOES have
- **UI Kit** → declarative UI via code
- **Custom UI** → full React UI
- CLI-based lifecycle (create, deploy, install)
- Native embedding into Jira / Confluence

👉 Forge optimizes for **professional developers**, not admins.

---

## 3️⃣ “But can a developer build GUI with Forge?” — YES

### Two developer-facing GUI paths

#### 🧩 UI Kit (code-defined GUI)
```js
<Text>Risk Score: High</Text>
<Button>Approve</Button>
```
- Simple
- Fast
- Secure
- No CSS

Used when:
- Forms
- Config screens
- Panels
- Admin views

---

#### 🎨 Custom UI (full React GUI)
```jsx
function App() {
  return <Dashboard />;
}
```
- Full React
- Charts, tables, AI panels
- Rich UX
- Looks like a real app

Used when:
- Dashboards
- AI copilots
- Risk engines
- Review & decision tools

---

## 4️⃣ Why Atlassian did NOT copy Salesforce’s GUI builder

This is intentional:

| Reason | Atlassian rationale |
|---|---|
| Security | Code + scopes are auditable |
| Consistency | UX aligns with Jira/Confluence |
| Scale | Marketplace-grade apps |
| Control | No fragile metadata soup |
| Dev quality | Fewer “accidental” apps |

> Forge is designed for **apps**, not **config hacks**.

---

## 5️⃣ Practical truth (important)

> **Forge GUIs are not built by clicking.  
They are built by coding UI that renders inside Atlassian products.**

Once deployed:
- Users see buttons, panels, dashboards
- It feels native
- It behaves like a first-class Jira feature

The *developer experience* is code-first.  
The *user experience* is GUI-first.

---

## 6️⃣ When Salesforce-style GUI builders beat Forge

Salesforce wins when:
- Non-developers build apps
- Business admins own UI
- Heavy metadata customization
- Rapid internal CRUD apps

---

## 7️⃣ When Forge beats Salesforce model

Forge wins when:
- You’re building **Marketplace apps**
- Security & trust matter
- AI is embedded into workflow
- Apps must feel native
- Hackathons & production share same stack

---

## Bottom line (crisp)

- ❌ Forge ≠ Salesforce Lightning Builder  
- ✅ Forge = **code-first GUI development**
- Developers **absolutely build GUIs** with Forge
- Atlassian chose **engineering discipline over drag-and-drop**

Here’s a **clear, structured explanation of how *Atlassian billing & subscriptions* work** focusing on Rovo, Forge, Jira, Confluence and other products — based on the official Atlassian support and pricing documentation. citeturn0view0turn0search0

---

## 🧾 **1. Billing & Subscription Overview (Atlassian Cloud)**

Atlassian’s **billing hub** lets you manage all cloud subscriptions (Standard, Premium, Enterprise) for apps such as Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket, and others.  
You can:  
- **View your active subscriptions & current bill**  
- **Switch between monthly vs annual billing**  
- **Add/remove users** (affects billing)  
- **Change payment method or update tax information**  
- **Cancel or renew apps**  
All of this is done via your billing account in **admin.atlassian.com**. citeturn0search15

The main documentation page grouped these billing topics (subscriptions, plans, billing profiles, Marketplace apps, usage charges, Rovo billing, and more). citeturn0view0

---

## 📊 **2. How Atlassian Charges You**

### **Seat-based Billing**

For cloud products like **Jira & Confluence**, pricing is **per user** — the more users you have, the higher the bill.  
- **Monthly** or **Annual** payment cycles available.  
- Price is based on the **maximum number of users in the billing period**.  
  That means if you add users mid-month, you pay for the highest user count that month (Maximum Quantity Billing). citeturn0search1turn0search16

### **Plan Levels**

Products often come in tiers:  
- **Free** — limited users/features  
- **Standard** — core functionality  
- **Premium** — more controls, SLAs, storage, analytics  
- **Enterprise** — custom pricing / advanced enterprise features citeturn0search2

---

## 🔹 **3. Jira (Core Product)**

**Jira Cloud** pricing is user-based and progressive — higher headcount often unlocks volume discounts, but billing always aligns to user seats within your plan.  
- Applies to **Jira Software**, **Jira Service Management**, and unified modern “Jira” offerings.  
- You’re charged monthly or annually per user seat.  
- Billing includes seat changes prorated across billing cycle. citeturn0search3turn0search16

**Note:** *Jira Work Management* has been merged into core Jira in recent changes, with its users consolidated — but billing remains under your Jira subscription. citeturn0search10

---

## 📘 **4. Confluence**

**Confluence Cloud** also uses a per-user pricing model with tiered plans: Free, Standard and Premium available.  
- Free plans are perpetual for small teams (up to 10 users).  
- For paid plans, you’re billed per user per month/year.  
- Higher tiers add more storage, admin controls, scale. citeturn0search2

---

## 🤖 **5. Rovo (Atlassian AI)**

Rovo is Atlassian’s integrated **AI layer** (search, chat, agents).  

**Current billing model:**
- Rovo *is included* with **Jira, Confluence, JSM or Teamwork Collection cloud plans** — no separate subscription line item for most users. citeturn0search19  
- Initially rolled out at no extra cost; usage charges may apply beyond quotas in future. citeturn0search11  
- If charges *do* occur (advanced usage beyond included), Rovo will appear on your bill as separate entries.

So **you don’t pay separately for Rovo** unless you exceed included usage; it’s tied to your main product subscription. citeturn0search19

---

## ⚙️ **6. Forge Platform**

**Forge** is a developer platform for building and running **cloud apps** within the Atlassian ecosystem:  
- Pricing is **consumption-based** — you pay based on actual usage of hosted functions, storage, APIs, etc. citeturn0search4  
- Many features are **free within generous limits**, and costs apply only when you exceed those. citeturn0search4  

This is different from seat-based billing for core products like Jira/Confluence — Forge costs are tied to **resource usage**, not number of users.

---

## 🧩 **7. Marketplace Add-ons**

Apps from the **Atlassian Marketplace** (e.g., portfolio boards, reporting extensions) are billed based on:  
- Number of users  
- Same billing cycle as your host product (Jira or Confluence).  
Installing an app *after* joining a collection may base billing on the collection’s total user count. citeturn0search17

---

## 📦 **8. Collections (Bundles)**

Atlassian offers **Collections** (e.g. Teamwork Collection, combining Jira + Confluence + other tools).  
- Instead of paying separately for each product, you receive a **single billable line item** for the bundle.  
- This simplifies invoicing and may reduce overall costs. citeturn0search8

---

## 🧠 **9. Summary: Product Billing Models**

| Product / Feature | Billing Model | Notes |
|------------------|---------------|-------|
| **Jira Cloud** | Seat-based subscription | Monthly/annual |
| **Confluence Cloud** | Seat-based subscription | Tiered plans |
| **Jira Service Management** | Seat/agent-based | Similar model |
| **Rovo** | Included + consumption | Often free unless over quota |
| **Forge** | Usage-based / consumption | Not tied to user seats |
| **Marketplace apps** | Seat-based | Matches host app billing |
| **Collections** | Single bundle billing | Consolidated invoices |

---

**Trello — What it is, Billing, How & When to Use**

image_group{"query":["Trello board example","Trello kanban cards","Trello workspace overview","Trello automation Butler"]}

---

## 🧩 What is **entity["company","Trello","atlassian kanban tool"]**?

**Trello** is a **visual task-management tool** based on the **Kanban** method.  
Work is organised into:

- **Boards** → projects or areas of work  
- **Lists** → stages (To-Do, Doing, Done, etc.)  
- **Cards** → individual tasks  

It’s designed for **clarity, speed, and low overhead**, not heavy process control.

Trello is owned by **entity["company","Atlassian","software company"]**.

---

## 🧠 Core Concept (Mental Model)

> **If Jira is for process and governance, Trello is for flow and visibility.**

No workflows, no ticket states, no complex permissions by default — just move cards visually.

---

## 💳 Trello Billing (Cloud)

Trello uses **workspace-level, per-user billing**.

### 🔹 Plans (as of current Atlassian model)

| Plan | Cost | Who it’s for |
|----|----|----|
| **Free** | £0 | Individuals, light teams |
| **Standard** | ~£5/user/month | Small teams |
| **Premium** | ~£10/user/month | Teams needing views & controls |
| **Enterprise** | Custom | Large orgs, governance |

> Billing is **monthly or annual**.  
> Charged per **active user** in a workspace.

### What changes as you pay?

| Feature | Free | Standard | Premium |
|------|------|---------|---------|
| Boards | Unlimited | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Power-Ups (integrations) | Limited | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Views (Calendar, Timeline) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Automation (Butler) | Limited | More | More |
| Admin controls | Basic | Medium | Advanced |

---

## ⚙️ How to Use Trello (Practically)

### 1️⃣ Create a Board
Example:
```
Board: Hackathon – Codegeist 2025
```

### 2️⃣ Add Lists (Stages)
```
Ideas → In Progress → Review → Done
```

### 3️⃣ Add Cards (Tasks)
Each card can contain:
- Description
- Checklist
- Due date
- Labels (priority, type)
- Attachments
- Comments

### 4️⃣ Move Cards Visually
Drag cards across lists as work progresses.

---

## 🤖 Automation (Butler)

Trello includes **Butler automation**:
- “When card moved to Done → mark checklist complete”
- “Every Monday → create weekly planning card”
- “When due date is today → send notification”

No coding required.

---

## 🧩 Integrations (Power-Ups)

Trello connects with:
- Google Drive
- Slack
- GitHub
- Jira (one-way or two-way)
- Calendar tools

Power-Ups extend functionality **without changing Trello’s simplicity**.

---

## ❓ When Should You Use Trello?

### ✅ Use Trello when:
- You want **quick visual tracking**
- Team is **non-technical**
- Process is **lightweight**
- You don’t need strict workflows
- You want **personal or small-team planning**

**Typical use cases**
- Personal task tracking  
- Content calendars  
- Hackathon planning  
- Family / life planning  
- Early-stage startups  
- Marketing & ops teams  

---

## 🚫 When NOT to Use Trello

Avoid Trello if you need:
- Complex workflows
- Issue types, states, transitions
- SLA tracking
- Role-based permissions
- Enterprise reporting

➡️ In those cases, **entity["company","Jira","issue tracking software"]** is the right tool.

---

## 🔁 Trello vs Jira (Quick Comparison)

| Aspect | Trello | Jira |
|----|----|----|
| Learning curve | Very low | Medium–high |
| Setup time | Minutes | Hours/days |
| Best for | Flow | Process |
| Governance | Minimal | Strong |
| Hackathons | ✅ Excellent | ⚠️ Heavy |
| Enterprises | ❌ Limited | ✅ Ideal |

---

## 🧠 Strategic View (Neutral & Practical)

- Trello is **not a “lite Jira”**
- It’s a **different philosophy**:
  - Visibility > control  
  - Flow > governance  
  - Speed > compliance  

Many teams **start in Trello** and **graduate to Jira** as complexity grows.

---

If you want, partner, I can:
- Map **Trello → Jira migration** cleanly  
- Design a **hybrid Trello + Jira setup**  
- Recommend **exact plan** for your current hackathon / personal workflow

**Forge — What it is, Billing, How & When to Use**

image_group{"query":["Atlassian Forge architecture diagram","Forge app Jira UI extension","Forge functions serverless","Forge developer console"]}

---

## 🧩 What is **entity["software_platform","Forge","atlassian app platform"]**?

**Forge** is **Atlassian’s official cloud app development platform**.

It lets you **build, host, and run apps directly inside Atlassian products** like:
- **entity["company","Jira","issue tracking software"]**
- **entity["company","Confluence","team knowledge base"]**
- **entity["company","Jira Service Management","it service platform"]**
- **entity["company","Bitbucket","git repository hosting"]**

Think of Forge as:
> **“Serverless apps that live *inside* Atlassian.”**

No external servers. No infra management.

Owned and operated by **entity["company","Atlassian","software company"]**.

---

## 🧠 Core Idea (Mental Model)

> **If Jira is the system of record, Forge is how you extend Jira safely.**

Forge apps:
- Run in Atlassian’s cloud
- Use Atlassian-managed security
- Are permission-aware by default
- Can be distributed via Atlassian Marketplace

---

## 🧱 What Can You Build with Forge?

### 🔹 UI Extensions
- Custom Jira panels
- Issue glance views
- Confluence macros
- Admin screens

### 🔹 Backend Logic
- Event listeners (issue created, updated, transitioned)
- Automation logic
- API integrations
- Data processing

### 🔹 AI-Integrated Apps
- Apps that use **entity["company","Rovo","atlassian ai"]**
- Smart summarisation
- Risk detection
- Knowledge extraction

---

## 💳 Forge Billing (Very Important)

Forge **is NOT seat-based** like Jira or Confluence.

### ✅ Forge uses **consumption-based billing**

You are billed based on:
- **Function execution time**
- **Number of invocations**
- **Storage usage**
- **Outbound API calls**

---

### 🔹 Free Allowances (Generous)

Most Forge apps:
- Cost **£0** at small–medium scale
- Stay free during hackathons
- Stay free for internal tools

You only pay **if you exceed usage quotas**.

> This is why Forge is ideal for hackathons and prototypes.

---

### 🔸 Who Pays?

| Scenario | Who pays |
|------|------|
| Internal app | Your Atlassian org |
| Marketplace app | App developer (cost recovered via pricing) |

---

## ⚙️ How to Use Forge (Practically)

### 1️⃣ Install Forge CLI
```bash
npm install -g @forge/cli
```

---

### 2️⃣ Create an App
```bash
forge create
```
Choose:
- Jira / Confluence / JSM
- UI Kit or Custom UI

---

### 3️⃣ Write Logic
- Frontend: React-style components
- Backend: Node.js functions
- Permissions declared explicitly

---

### 4️⃣ Deploy
```bash
forge deploy
forge install
```

No servers. No Docker. No AWS setup.

---

### 5️⃣ Monitor
- Logs
- Invocation counts
- Errors
via Forge console.

---

## 🔐 Security & Governance (Key Differentiator)

Forge provides:
- Automatic sandboxing
- Strict permission scopes
- Data residency controls
- Atlassian-managed auth

> Forge is designed so enterprises **trust apps by default**.

This is the **main reason Atlassian pushes Forge over Connect**.

---

## 🔁 Forge vs Connect (Short)

| Aspect | Forge | Connect |
|----|----|----|
| Hosting | Atlassian | You |
| Infra mgmt | ❌ None | ✅ Required |
| Security | Built-in | Your responsibility |
| Billing | Usage-based | Infra + ops |
| Hackathons | ✅ Ideal | ❌ Heavy |

---

## ❓ When Should You Use Forge?

### ✅ Use Forge when:
- Building apps *inside* Jira / Confluence
- You want zero infrastructure
- Security & compliance matter
- You’re targeting Marketplace
- You’re in hackathons (Codegeist)

**Typical use cases**
- Risk detection apps
- Workflow automation
- AI copilots
- Reporting panels
- Compliance tools
- Knowledge summarisation

---

## 🚫 When NOT to Use Forge

Avoid Forge if:
- You need full custom backend control
- You require long-running processes
- You need heavy compute workloads

In those cases, external services may fit better.

---

## 🧠 Strategic Guidance (Neutral, Practical)

- Forge = **extension layer**, not a full platform
- Optimised for **product-native apps**
- Perfect for **ROVO-first AI apps**
- Low cost, high trust, fast delivery

---

If you want, partner, I can:
- Design a **Forge app architecture** for your use case  
- Explain **exact cost scenarios** (calls → £)  
- Map **Forge + Rovo + Jira** cleanly for Codegeist

## 🧩 What is **entity["company","Confluence","team knowledge base"]**?

**Confluence** is a **collaborative documentation and knowledge-management system**.

Think of it as:
> **A shared, living wiki for teams and organisations**

It’s where teams **write, organise, and preserve knowledge** — decisions, specs, meeting notes, runbooks, policies, and architecture docs.

Confluence is owned by **entity["company","Atlassian","software company"]**.

---

## 🧠 Core Idea (Mental Model)

> **If Jira tracks work, Confluence explains work.**

Jira answers *“What’s happening?”*  
Confluence answers *“Why, how, and what we decided.”*

---

## 🧱 Core Building Blocks

| Concept | Meaning |
|------|------|
| **Space** | A knowledge area (project, team, domain) |
| **Page** | A document |
| **Hierarchy** | Pages can have parents/children |
| **Templates** | Pre-structured pages |
| **Comments** | Discussion on content |
| **Permissions** | Control who can see/edit |

---

## 💳 Confluence Billing (Cloud)

Confluence uses **seat-based subscription billing**, like Jira.

### 🔹 Plans

| Plan | Who it’s for |
|----|----|
| **Free** | Individuals / very small teams |
| **Standard** | Most teams |
| **Premium** | Scale & controls |
| **Enterprise** | Large orgs |

- **Monthly or Annual billing**
- Charged per **user seat**
- You pay for the **maximum number of users** during the billing period

---

### 🔢 What Changes Between Plans

| Feature | Free | Standard | Premium |
|------|------|----------|---------|
| Max users | ~10 | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Storage | Limited | Higher | Much higher |
| Page history | Limited | Full | Advanced |
| Permissions | Basic | Advanced | Advanced |
| Admin controls | Basic | More | More |
| Analytics | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

---

## ⚙️ How to Use Confluence (Practically)

### 1️⃣ Create Spaces
Example spaces:
- Project Docs
- Engineering Wiki
- Product Decisions
- Operations Manual

---

### 2️⃣ Create Pages
Pages can include:
- Rich text
- Tables
- Images
- Code blocks
- Diagrams
- Attachments

---

### 3️⃣ Use Templates
Common templates:
- Meeting notes
- Decision log
- Product requirements
- Architecture design
- Runbooks

Templates ensure **consistency**.

---

### 4️⃣ Collaborate
- Multiple users edit at once
- Inline comments
- @mentions
- Page version history

---

## 🔗 Jira ↔ Confluence Integration

This is where Confluence shines.

You can:
- Embed Jira issues into pages
- Auto-generate docs from Jira projects
- Link specs directly to execution

Together:
- Jira = execution  
- Confluence = knowledge

---

## ❓ When Should You Use Confluence?

### ✅ Use Confluence when:
- Knowledge must **outlive people**
- Decisions need documentation
- Onboarding new members
- Running distributed teams
- You want **one source of truth**

**Typical use cases**
- Project documentation
- Product specs
- Architecture docs
- Meeting notes
- Policies & SOPs
- Hackathon submissions (narrative)

---

## 🚫 When NOT to Use Confluence

Avoid Confluence if:
- You just need quick notes
- Docs are personal, not shared
- Team is very small & informal

➡️ In that case, a simple notes app may suffice.

---

## 🔁 Confluence vs Jira vs Trello

| Tool | Best for | Purpose |
|----|----|----|
| **Confluence** | Knowledge | Explain & preserve |
| **Jira** | Execution | Track & govern |
| **Trello** | Flow | Visual tasks |

---

## 🧠 Strategic Guidance (Neutral)

- Use Confluence as **institutional memory**
- Don’t let docs rot — link them to Jira
- Write once, reuse forever

---

If you want, partner, I can:
- Design a **minimal Confluence space structure**
- Create **ready-to-use templates**
- Map your **hackathon / project docs** cleanly into Confluence

## 🧩 What is **entity["company","Bitbucket","git repository hosting"]**?

**Bitbucket** is a **Git-based source code repository and collaboration platform**.

It is used to:
- Store source code securely
- Manage branches
- Review code via pull requests
- Run CI/CD pipelines
- Control access and permissions

Bitbucket is built for **professional teams**, especially those already using Jira.

It is owned by **entity["company","Atlassian","software company"]**.

---

## 🧠 Core Idea (Mental Model)

> **If Jira tracks work, Bitbucket holds the code that does the work.**

Jira = *what*  
Bitbucket = *how (code)*

---

## 🧱 Core Building Blocks

| Concept | Meaning |
|------|------|
| **Repository** | Codebase |
| **Branch** | Parallel line of development |
| **Commit** | Code change |
| **Pull Request (PR)** | Code review & merge |
| **Pipeline** | Automated build/test/deploy |
| **Permissions** | Who can read/write/merge |

---

## 💳 Bitbucket Billing (Cloud)

Bitbucket uses **user-based + usage-based billing**.

### 🔹 Plans

| Plan | Who it’s for |
|----|----|
| **Free** | Small teams |
| **Standard** | Growing teams |
| **Premium** | Advanced controls |

Billing includes:
- **User seats** (developers with access)
- **CI/CD minutes** (Bitbucket Pipelines)
- **Storage limits**

You pay monthly or annually.

---

### 🔢 What Changes Between Plans

| Feature | Free | Standard | Premium |
|------|------|----------|---------|
| Max users | Small | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Private repos | Limited | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Pipelines minutes | Limited | More | More |
| Merge checks | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| IP allowlisting | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Advanced permissions | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

---

## ⚙️ How to Use Bitbucket (Step-by-Step)

- Choose Git
- Set visibility (private/public)


---

### 3️⃣ Create Branches
Common strategy:
```

develop
feature/xyz
```

---

### 4️⃣ Commit & Push
```bash

git commit -m "Implement feature X"

```

---

### 5️⃣ Pull Requests (PRs)
- Request review
- Run checks
- Merge safely

---

### 6️⃣ Pipelines (CI/CD)
Automate:
- Build
- Test
- Lint
- Deploy

Example use cases:
- Deploy on merge
- Run tests on every PR

---

## 🔗 Jira ↔ Bitbucket Integration

- Link commits to Jira issues
- Auto-update issue status on PR merge
- Trace work → code → deployment

This gives **end-to-end traceability**.

---

## ❓ When Should You Use Bitbucket?

### ✅ Use Bitbucket when:
- You’re building software
- Team needs code review
- CI/CD is required
- Access control matters
- You already use Jira

**Typical use cases**
- Product development
- Internal tools
- APIs & services
- Hackathon codebases
- Enterprise software

---

## 🚫 When NOT to Use Bitbucket

Avoid Bitbucket if:
- You don’t write code
- You want social/open-source visibility first (GitHub may fit better)
- You don’t need pipelines or Jira integration

---

## 🔁 Bitbucket vs GitHub vs GitLab

| Platform | Best for |
|----|----|
| **Bitbucket** | Jira-first teams |
| **GitHub** | Open source & community |
| **GitLab** | All-in-one DevOps |

---

## 🧠 Strategic Guidance (Neutral)

- Bitbucket excels in **controlled, enterprise-friendly environments**
- Not about popularity — about **governance + traceability**
- Best value when combined with Jira

---

- Set up **Pipelines templates**

I’ll map a concrete example app: **“Risk Intake + Scoring + Approval + Dashboard”**  
(That’s a good analog for both ecosystems.)

---

## A) Build it in Salesforce (Lightning + Apex) — step-by-step

### 1) Data model
1. Create a **Custom Object**: `Risk__c`
2. Add fields: `Title`, `Description`, `Severity`, `Owner`, `Status`, `Score`, `Approver`, `Evidence`, etc.
3. Configure **relationships** if needed (e.g., `Project__c` lookup)

### 2) UI (admin-friendly / low-code)
4. Use **Lightning App Builder** to create:
   - Record page layout for `Risk__c`
   - Custom page tabs (Risk Console, Approvals, etc.)
   - Visibility rules (show components by profile/field values) citeturn0search15turn0search19

### 3) Workflow automation
5. Use **Flow** / Process tools (common) for:
   - Auto-assigning approver
   - Notifications
   - Status changes
6. Add **Approval Process** (if needed) for formal approval routing

### 4) Code logic (when low-code isn’t enough)
7. Create **Apex Trigger** on `Risk__c`:
   - Before insert/update → compute `Score`
   - After update → create tasks / callouts / audit events citeturn0search5turn0search20

### 5) Reporting / dashboards
8. Create reports + dashboards (Risk by severity, aging, SLA breaches, etc.)

### 6) Deploy & govern
9. Package / deploy via metadata pipeline
10. Control access using profiles, permission sets, field-level security

**Developer experience summary:** Salesforce lets admins build a lot via GUI builder + metadata, then Apex for “hard logic”.

---

## B) Build it in Forge (Jira/Confluence app) — step-by-step

### 1) “Data model” equivalent (inside Jira)
1. Decide where “Risk” lives:
   - Usually as a **Jira issue type**: `Risk`
2. Add Jira **custom fields**: Severity, Score, Approver, Evidence, etc.
3. Decide workflow: `Draft → Review → Approved/Rejected → Closed`

*(In Atlassian, much of the “object model” is Jira configuration + issue fields.)*

### 2) UI inside Jira (real embedded GUI)
4. Build a UI surface like a **Jira Issue Panel**:
   - Show Risk Score, explanation, actions (Approve/Reject), audit trail citeturn0search2
5. Choose UI approach:
   - **UI Kit** (fast, native-looking components) citeturn0search0turn0search21  
   - **Custom UI** (full React/CSS dashboard; runs in iframe sandbox) citeturn0search6turn0search12

### 3) Event-driven automation (the “trigger” equivalent)
6. Add Forge **Triggers** to react to Jira events:
   - On issue created/updated/transitioned → recompute score, tag, comment, etc. citeturn0search13
7. If you need periodic checks (aging risks, SLA sweeps):
   - Use **Scheduled Trigger** (hour/day/week) citeturn0search1
8. If you need an inbound endpoint (webhook from outside):
   - Use **Web Trigger** citeturn0search17

### 4) Storage
9. Persist app-specific data using **Forge storage** (KV store / hosted storage) citeturn0search23  
   (Example: scoring history snapshots, model versions, configuration)

### 5) Deploy & operate
10. Use Forge tooling (CLI) to deploy/install (devs do this; end users never see it)
11. Monitor usage/costs via Forge usage metrics citeturn0search11

### 6) Billing (important difference)
12. Forge is **consumption-based** (compute/storage/invocations), with a generous free allowance; Atlassian has announced/implemented consumption pricing timing and rules around 2026. citeturn0search4turn0search8turn0search14

**Developer experience summary:** Forge is code-first for UI + logic (UI Kit/Custom UI + triggers), running inside Jira/Confluence with Atlassian-managed hosting.

---

## The cleanest 1:1 mapping table

| What you’re building | Salesforce way | Forge (Jira) way |
|---|---|---|
| Data entity | Custom Object | Issue type + custom fields |
| UI builder | Lightning App Builder (drag-drop) citeturn0search15turn0search19 | UI Kit / Custom UI in Jira panel citeturn0search2turn0search6 |

| Inbound endpoint | Apex REST | Forge Web Trigger citeturn0search17 |
| Hosting | Salesforce-managed | Atlassian-managed |
| Cost model | Platform licensing | Forge consumption pricing citeturn0search4turn0search8 |

---

## Practical takeaway
- If your goal is **admin-built apps** (drag/drop, metadata-first), Salesforce is built for that. citeturn0search15turn0search19  
- If your goal is **embedded product extensions** inside Jira/Confluence (panel, workflow triggers, native UX), Forge is built for that. citeturn0search2turn0search13turn0search6

**Forge vs Salesforce Apex — CLI, GUI, and “is a UI even useful?”**

image_group{"query":["Atlassian Forge architecture diagram","Forge UI Kit Jira example","Forge Custom UI React","Salesforce Apex Lightning architecture diagram"]}

---

## Short answer (direct)

- **Forge ≠ Salesforce Apex**, but they play a **similar role** in their ecosystems.  
- **Forge is NOT only CLI** — CLI is just the *developer entry*.  
- **Yes, GUI in Forge is very useful** — *when it’s the right kind of GUI*.

Now the precise breakdown 👇

---

## 1️⃣ Is Forge the same as Salesforce Apex?

### ❌ Not the same  
### ✅ Similar *conceptual role*

| Aspect | **entity["software_platform","Forge","atlassian app platform"]** | **entity["software_platform","Salesforce Apex","salesforce server language"]** |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Extend Atlassian products | Extend Salesforce |
| Language | JavaScript / Node.js | Apex (Java-like) |
| Execution | Serverless functions | Managed runtime |
| Security | Permission scopes | Governor limits |
| Deployment | CLI-based | UI + metadata deploy |
| Infra | Atlassian-managed | Salesforce-managed |

### Mental model
> **Apex is Salesforce’s internal language**  
> **Forge is Atlassian’s external extension platform**

Forge is *closer to* **Salesforce Lightning + Apex together**, not Apex alone.

---

## 2️⃣ Is Forge “only CLI”?

### ❌ No  
### ✅ CLI is just the *entry point*

The **Forge CLI** is used for:
- Creating apps
- Declaring permissions
- Deploying code
- Installing apps

But **users never see the CLI**.

### What users see instead
- Jira panels
- Issue sidebars
- Admin screens
- Confluence macros
- Dialogs & modals

👉 These are **GUIs rendered inside Jira / Confluence**.

---

## 3️⃣ GUI in Forge — is it useful or pointless?

### 🔥 Very useful — *but only for certain jobs*

Forge GUIs are **embedded UIs**, not full standalone apps.

### Two UI models in Forge

#### 🧩 UI Kit
- Declarative
- Simple components
- Fast to build
- Limited styling

Best for:
- Admin panels
- Issue glances
- Settings screens

---

#### 🎨 Custom UI
- Full React
- Your own CSS
- Rich interactions
- Uses iframe sandbox

Best for:
- Dashboards
- AI assistants
- Risk analysis views
- Data-heavy panels

---

## 4️⃣ When a Forge GUI is **high-value**

### ✅ Use GUI when:
- Human decision is involved
- Output needs explanation
- AI results must be reviewed
- Admins need configuration
- Users need trust & visibility

**Examples**
- Risk scoring panel in Jira
- AI-generated summary with “Accept / Reject”
- Compliance checklist UI
- Project health dashboard

---

## 5️⃣ When GUI is **not needed**

### ❌ Skip GUI when:
- App is fully event-driven
- Pure automation
- Background processing
- Silent enrichment

**Examples**
- Auto-label issues
- Auto-create tasks
- Sync data
- Background AI classification

These run **headless** via Forge functions.

---

## 6️⃣ Forge vs Salesforce Lightning (closest comparison)

| Dimension | Forge | Salesforce Lightning |
|---|---|---|
| UI embedding | Inside Jira/Confluence | Inside Salesforce |
| Backend logic | Forge functions | Apex |
| Security | Scope-based | Governor limits |
| Deployment | CLI | Metadata deploy |
| Marketplace | Atlassian Marketplace | AppExchange |

👉 **Forge = Lightning Components + Serverless Apex**, conceptually.

---

## 7️⃣ Strategic clarity (important)

> Forge is **not** meant to replace:
- Full web apps
- Heavy backend systems
- Long-running processes

Forge **is meant to**:
- Extend Atlassian UX
- Inject logic at the right moment
- Add AI + automation *where work already happens*

---

## Bottom line (crisp)

- Forge ≠ Apex, but **same ecosystem role**
- CLI is **developer tooling only**
- GUI in Forge is **highly valuable** when:
  - Humans must see / decide / trust
- Forge shines in **embedded intelligence**, not standalone apps

---

- Map **Forge vs Apex vs Lightning** using a single architecture example  
- Tell you **exactly when NOT to build a Forge UI**  
- Design a **ROVO + Forge UI pattern** for your current Jira app

**Jira — What it is, Billing, How & When to Use**

image_group{"query":["Jira Software board scrum","Jira kanban board example","Jira issue workflow diagram","Jira backlog sprint view"]}

---

## 🧩 What is **entity["company","Jira","issue tracking software"]**?

**Jira** is a **work management and issue-tracking system** designed for **structured, repeatable work**.

It was originally built for **software teams**, but today it’s used across:
- Engineering
- IT & service desks
- Product management
- Operations
- Risk & compliance teams

Jira is owned by **entity["company","Atlassian","software company"]**.

---

## 🧠 Core Idea (Mental Model)

> **Jira is a system of record.**  
> It answers: *Who is doing what, in which state, under which rules, with what history.*

Unlike Trello’s free-flow cards, Jira enforces **structure**.

---

## 🧱 Core Building Blocks

| Concept | Meaning |
|------|------|
| **Project** | Container for work |
| **Issue** | A unit of work (task, bug, story, risk, etc.) |
| **Issue Types** | Different kinds of work |
| **Workflow** | States + transitions |
| **Board** | Visual view (Scrum / Kanban) |
| **Backlog** | Ordered future work |

---

## 💳 Jira Billing (Cloud)

Jira uses **seat-based subscription billing**.

### 🔹 Plans

| Plan | Typical Use |
|----|----|
| **Free** | Small teams |
| **Standard** | Most teams |
| **Premium** | Scale, controls |
| **Enterprise** | Large orgs |

Billing options:
- **Monthly or Annual**
- Charged per **user seat**
- Cost increases as user count increases

> You pay for the **maximum number of users** in a billing period.

---

### 🔢 What Changes Between Plans

| Feature | Free | Standard | Premium |
|------|------|----------|---------|
| Max users | ~10 | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| Workflows | Basic | Custom | Advanced |
| Automation | Limited | More | More |
| Permissions | Basic | Advanced | Advanced |
| Storage | Low | Medium | High |
| SLA / Scale | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

---

## ⚙️ How to Use Jira (Step-by-Step)

### 1️⃣ Create a Project
Choose project type:
- **Scrum** (time-boxed sprints)
- **Kanban** (continuous flow)
- **Business / Ops** (non-dev work)

---

### 2️⃣ Define Issue Types
Common ones:
- Story
- Task
- Bug
- Epic
- Risk
- Incident

---

### 3️⃣ Design Workflow
Example:
```
To Do → In Progress → Review → Done
```
(With rules: who can move what, when)

---

### 4️⃣ Plan Work
- Add issues to **Backlog**
- Prioritise
- Assign owners
- Set due dates

---

### 5️⃣ Track Execution
- Boards show live status
- Filters and dashboards show progress
- History is always preserved

---

## 🤖 Automation & AI

- Built-in **rules engine** (if X then Y)
- **entity["company","Rovo","atlassian ai"]** adds:
  - Natural-language search
  - AI summaries
  - Smart recommendations

---

## ❓ When Should You Use Jira?

### ✅ Use Jira when:
- Work is **complex or regulated**
- Multiple people depend on states
- You need **audit trails**
- Work repeats every sprint/month
- You need reports & metrics

**Typical use cases**
- Software development
- Incident & bug tracking
- Compliance tracking
- Risk management
- Change management
- Enterprise operations

---

## 🚫 When NOT to Use Jira

Avoid Jira if:
- You want quick, informal task tracking
- Team is non-technical and small
- Process overhead slows you down

➡️ In those cases, **entity["company","Trello","kanban tool"]** is better.

---

## 🔁 Jira vs Trello (Quick View)

| Dimension | Jira | Trello |
|----|----|----|
| Structure | High | Low |
| Governance | Strong | Minimal |
| Learning curve | Medium | Very low |
| Best for | Process | Flow |
| Audits & history | ✅ | ❌ |
| Hackathons | ⚠️ Heavy | ✅ Light |

---

## 🧠 Strategic Guidance (Neutral)

- Start with **Jira only when structure is needed**
- Don’t over-engineer small teams
- Jira shines when **coordination > speed**

---

- Recommend **exact Jira plan** for your use case  
- Design a **minimal Jira setup** (no bloat)  
- Map **Trello → Jira** cleanly for scale
